analysis.title: GS - Jeter - Earnings Recap - 28 Oct 2026
key_insights: TMT: SK Hynix 3Q operating profit beat (W83.3tn vs BBGe W76.9tn and GSe W77.5tn) opened mildly on a W20tn buyback below the W30tn-W40tn the Street expected, then recovered on the call. Management said the memory shortage should last through 2030, DRAM capacity is largely sold out through 2029, and LTAs cover over 50% of 2027-2028 capacity.

Samsung Electronics (SEC) holds its 3Q call tomorrow at 10am KST, where investors want more detail on shareholder returns. Foreigners and local institutions were joint net buyers of Hynix and Samsung while retail sold.

ETSY beat and raised. Marketplace GMS grew +9.1% y/y cc (from +7.2%), EBITDA margin was 30.4%, active buyers grew y/y for the first time in 2 years, and the FY GMS guide rose to ~7% y/y. The stock hit a new 52-week high and a CFO change was announced.

TER reported revenue of $1.31bn and non-GAAP EPS of $2.29, ahead of GS ($2.15) and the Street ($2.05). 4Q EPS guide midpoint of $2.10 is above the Street's $2.05, but expectations were elevated going in. Robotics revenue missed ($96mn vs GS $105mn).

STX beat slightly (revenue $4.23bn, operating EPS $7.68) and guided 2Q well above the Street (revenue $4.80bn vs Street $4.50bn, EPS $9.20 vs $8.54, operating margin mid-50%). Price per exabyte rose ~33% y/y and management expects strong pricing through FY27. GS tags the print (-) because expectations were elevated after WDC.

Industrials/Energy, power and data center names were strong. VRT beat on EPS ($2.21 vs $1.82) and revenue ($4.3bn vs $3.75bn) with Americas organic growth at 66% and 100% order growth. GEV beat on revenue and EBITDA, lifted FY guidance, raised its buyback to $20bn from $10bn and announced a $9bn Trench Group acquisition. AEP signed 15 GW of new load commitments in 3Q and sees contracted load reaching 84 GW by 2031.

PUMP beat on 3Q adj EBITDA ($60mn vs $53mn) and service revenue. Power generation capacity under contract reached 510 MW and the company is negotiating several hundred megawatts of data center opportunities.

Refiners posted large beats. DINO adj EPS was $11.75 vs $8.18 and PSX adj EPS was $14.08 vs $12.08 with refining margin of $38/bbl vs $36.18. DINO was described as one of the more crowded longs in Refining into the print, and it named a new CEO.

Oilfield services and E&Ps were mixed. BKR beat 3Q but guided 4Q revenue and EBITDA below the Street, citing Middle East disruptions, while FY IET orders were raised to $21.5-$23.5bn. EXE and EQT beat EPS. RRC beat and holds no call given the proposed EQT merger. FCX beat but raised capex guidance to $4.4bn.

Cost inflation and soft demand hit several industrials. LII cut FY EPS guidance to $21-$21.50 from $23-$24. OI missed and cut FY guidance with a 16% implied move. SW cut FY EBITDA to ~$4.7bn from $5-5.3bn. LSTR missed on elevated insurance costs. DAN cut FY EPS guidance. ENPH missed and guided 4Q revenue to $225-$255mn vs $298.8mn consensus.

Other industrial beats and raises: PPG (EPS $2.25 vs $2.12, raised outlook), MAS, FTV, CLH, LFUS (Q4 EPS guide way above), AER (EPS $6.56 vs $4.56), CR, TEL (fiscal Q1 EPS guide $3.30 vs $3), IEX, KEX and CSTM. WERN missed but had pre-announced.

Financials: JLL beat with double-digit beats in Leasing Advisory and capital markets and raised 2026 adj EPS guide to $25.2-26.3. EVR had a 70% earnings beat and 32% revenue beat with comp ratio down 50bps QoQ. AON showed organic growth at least ~1pt above expectations in all 4 segments, and GS sees positioning as ignored rather than shorted.

Financials, mixed names: V beat narrowly with FY27 net revenue growth guided to low double digits, which GS called in line. LPLA beat 5% on EPS but organic growth slipped (September NNA below 4%). HOOD beat core EPS by 1c but October equity, options and crypto volumes are tracking ~5% below 3Q26 and it missed on Monthly Active Users. RNR beat on EPS but BVPS fell $7-8 short on an AOCI hit.

REITs: EXR raised FY26 core FFO guide midpoint to $8.45 (vs $8.36 cons) on lower property operating costs. BXP beat FFO ($1.89 vs $1.80) with occupancy up 100bps sequentially to 89.4%. ESS missed core FFO by 1c with weaker new lease growth (-0.2%).

Consumer: EAT stock had fallen from $260 in August to ~$195-$200 into the print, then reported comps of +9.1% vs +7.5%, EPS $2.77 vs $2.45 and raised FY EPS guide to $13.30-$13.90. CAKE comps of +15.2% vs +7% were strong but expectations were high. VFC beat (EPS $0.70 vs $0.54) but Vans fell 10% and Active missed. CZR missed adj EBITDA ($865M vs $931M) with Las Vegas down ~9% y/y, and GS sees a slightly negative read-across for MGM. JMKE comps of +3% were at the low end and the FY comp guide was cut.

Healthcare: GEHC beat and raised (revenue $5.5B vs $5.35B, organic +6.2% vs 3.5%, EPS guide $4.95-$5.05). ICLR book-to-bill was 1.56x vs 1.3x and guidance was raised. BIIB beat on Spinraza. BBNX narrowed its guide up but withdrew its 3D Intelligence 510(k). BSX cut 2026 organic guidance to ~3.75% from 5-6% and guided 4Q organic growth to -3% to -1%, citing a cyber security incident. UHS missed adjusted EBITDA-NCI ($624.6mn vs $633.5mn Street) on lower revenue per adjusted admission and higher operating expenses.

earnings_insights: SK Hynix 3Q operating profit W83.3tn (reported) vs BBGe W76.9tn and GSe W77.5tn (estimates). Buyback W20tn vs Street W30tn-W40tn expected.
ETSY: reported marketplace GMS +9.1% y/y cc vs +7.2% last quarter, EBITDA margin 30.4%. FY GMS guide ~7% y/y vs prior ~MSDs, EBITDA margin guide 30% vs prior 29-30%.

TER: reported revenue $1.31bn (GS est $1.30bn, Street est $1.27bn), non-GAAP EPS $2.29 (GS est $2.15, Street est $2.05). 4Q non-GAAP EPS guide $1.95-$2.25, midpoint $2.10 vs GS est $2.03 and Street est $2.05.
STX: reported F1Q revenue $4.23bn (Street est $4.14bn), operating EPS $7.68 (Street est $7.42). F2Q guide revenue $4.80bn midpoint (Street est $4.50bn), operating EPS $9.20 (Street est $8.54).
VRT: reported Q3 EPS $2.21 vs $1.82 consensus, revenue $4.3bn vs $3.75bn. Q4 guide EPS $2.22-2.28 vs $2.21 consensus, revenue $4.31-4.5bn vs $4.3bn.

GEV: reported Q3 revenue $12.64bn vs $12bn, EBITDA $1.94bn vs $1.68bn, EPS $4.81 vs $4.01 (the report writes this as '$4.01bn'). FY guide sales $47bn (consensus $46bn), EBITDA $6.6bn (consensus $6.34bn), FCF $16-17bn.
PPG: reported Q3 EPS $2.25 vs $2.12 consensus, revenue $4.35bn vs $4.27bn. FY outlook $7.90-8.10 vs $7.89 consensus and $7.70-8.10 prior.
DINO: reported 3Q adj EPS $11.75 vs Street $8.18, adj EBITDA $2.98bn vs $2.11bn. PSX: reported 3Q adj EPS $14.08 vs Street $12.08.
AER: reported Q3 EPS $6.56 vs $4.56 consensus, revenue $2.42bn vs $2.15bn. FY guide $20.70 vs $16.80 prior.
LII: reported EPS $6.84 vs $7.36 consensus. FY EPS guide lowered to $21-$21.50 vs prior $23-$24.
OI: reported Q3 EPS loss of 9c vs $0.16 positive consensus, EBITDA $234mm vs $263mm. FY EBITDA guide $925-950mm vs $1-1.1bn prior.
SW: reported Q3 EBITDA $1.21bn vs $1.3bn, EPS below $0.45 vs $0.57. FY EBITDA now ~$4.7bn vs $5-5.3bn prior.
ENPH: reported 3Q adj EPS $0.41 vs $0.51 consensus. 4Q revenue guide $225-$255mn vs $298.8mn consensus.
BKR: reported 3Q revenue $8.03bn vs Street $7.75bn, adj EBITDA $1.42bn vs $1.34bn. 4Q guide revenue $7.8-$8.7bn vs Street $8.3bn, adj EBITDA $1.325-$1.595bn vs Street $1.46bn.
TEL: reported Q4 EPS $3.14 vs $3.07. Fiscal Q1 guide EPS $3.30 vs $3 and revenue $5.35bn vs $5.14bn.
FTV: reported Q3 EPS $0.77 vs $0.70, guide raised to $3.10-3.14 from $2.95-3.05. CR: reported Q3 EPS $2.05 vs $1.82, FY guide raised to $7.23-7.38 from $6.85-7.05.
V: reported earnings $3.48 vs consensus $3.44. FY27 guide points to low double-digit net revenue growth and low double-digit to low-teens EPS growth.
HOOD: reported core EPS beat by 1c. October MTD event contracts tracking 10% above 3Q26 and equity, options and crypto volumes tracking ~5% below 3Q26.
RNR: reported EPS $12.72 vs $10.62 consensus, combined ratio 79.7% vs 83.3%. 3Q buyback $310mn in line with expectations.
EAT: reported 1Q EPS $2.77 vs $2.45 consensus, comps +9.1% vs +7.5%. FY EPS guide $13.30-$13.90 vs prior $12.60-$13.40.
CAKE: reported EPS $1.02 vs $0.96 consensus, comps +15.2% vs +7%. VFC: reported EPS $0.70 vs $0.54 cons, revenue $2.7B vs $2.67B.
CZR: reported adj EBITDA $865M vs $931M consensus and GS est $904M. Las Vegas $343M vs $387M cons.

GEHC: reported EPS $1.34 vs $1.20 cons, FY EPS guide $4.95 to $5.05 vs $4.80 to $5.00 prior. BSX: reported 3Q sales $5.14B vs $5.05B cons, EPS $0.73 in line, 4Q EPS guide $0.77 to $0.79 vs $0.84 cons.
UHS: reported 3Q26 revenue $4.733bn vs GS est $4.722bn and Street est $4.713bn, adjusted EBITDA-NCI $624.6mn vs GS est $670.4mn and Street est $633.5mn.
crypto_views: HOOD said October MTD equity, options and crypto volumes are tracking ~5% below 3Q26 levels.
risk_factors: Elevated expectations into prints (TER, STX, CAKE) limit upside even on beats.
Cost inflation, insurance costs and soft demand are pressuring industrial margins and guidance (LII, OI, LSTR, SW).
Rates: RNR book value was hit by AOCI losses from higher rates.
Cyber security incident at BSX muddies the 2026 and 4Q guide and the 2027 baseline.
Las Vegas weakness at CZR, with a slightly negative read-across for MGM.
Slower trading volumes at HOOD in October and a missed Monthly Active Users figure.
Pricing and mix pressure on UHS margins.
vol_and_positioning: Desk-stated implied earnings moves: OI 16%, DINO 8%, VRT 9%, PPG 3%, MAS 7%, HAYW 9%, ODFL 6%, FTV 9%, CLH 6%, LFUS 9%, TEL 8%, KEX 8%, SITE 9%, DAN 9%, NBR 10%, GNRC 8%, SW 6%.
DINO was one of the more crowded longs in Refining into the print from the dedicated community.
AON positioning described as 'ignored' with an 'absence of longs' rather than aggressively shorted. APAM positioning skewed negative within the group.
Specialists had been leaning cautious on EXE going in and expected capex to come in hotter. Specialists had been more cautious on OKE relative to TRGP and KNTK into the prints.
In Korea, foreigners and local institutions were net buyers of Hynix (+$288mn/+$177mn) and Samsung (+$280mn/+$297mn) while retail sold (-$463mn Hynix, -$564mn Samsung).
geopolitical: BKR's IET segment pointed to Middle East disruptions in its 4Q guidance, and OFSE expectations for 4Q reflect lower Middle East activity, consistent with 2Q levels.

tension_points.bull_case: Hynix management said the memory shortage lasts through 2030, DRAM capacity is sold out through 2029 and LTAs cover over 50% of 2027-2028 capacity. Seagate guided 2Q far above the Street with ~33% y/y price per exabyte growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Hynix opened mildly because its W20tn buyback was below the W30tn-W40tn expected, and STX is tagged negative because expectations were elevated following WDC.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Samsung's 3Q earnings call tomorrow at 10am KST with additional details on shareholder returns.

tension_points.bull_case: CAKE comps of +15.2% vs +7% consensus and EAT comps of +9.1% vs +7.5% with a raised FY EPS guide.
tension_points.bear_case: CAKE bogey was well into the double digits and a lot of upside was expected, so the question is how much was priced. EAT had already fallen from $260 to ~$195-$200 on slower recent data.
tension_points.what_invalidates: EAT exit trends and the start to fiscal 2Q, which is where a lot of investors were focused.

tension_points.bull_case: EVR had a 70% earnings beat, 32% revenue beat, comp ratio down 50bps QoQ and noncomp dollars down 5% QoQ.
tension_points.bear_case: Sentiment on the print was cautious and the results may be too big to be pull-forward, with concern around noncomp trajectory among boutiques.
tension_points.what_invalidates: How management contextualizes near-term pipelines on the call.
